business_question: When planning, before loading, which lane and vehicle choices end up below 60% full?

base_rate_or_baseline.metric: PR-AUC of constant base rate (= test prevalence)

extra_baselines.name: Lookup route×vehicle_type, rates fitted on TRAIN shipments only (<5 rows -> train base rate)
extra_baselines.note: rates fitted on training shipments only

winner_reason: LightGBM chosen on PR-AUC (0.7516); models within 2% of the best: ['LightGBM'] (simplest preferred).

top_drivers.plain_english: origin_plant: the biggest push toward under-loading risk comes from '39TT', the biggest push away from it from '3902'.
route: the biggest push toward under-loading risk comes from 'SAMANR', the biggest push away from it from 'GCHAZ2'.
destination_point: the biggest push toward under-loading risk comes from 'HAZIRA', the biggest push away from it from 'KALUAKURTY'.
vehicle_type: the biggest push toward under-loading risk comes from 'SB06', the biggest push away from it from 'OB13'.
vendor: the biggest push toward under-loading risk comes from 'V066', the biggest push away from it from 'V005'.

caveats: 560 exact duplicate rows (all 69 columns equal; ₹1.1 Cr of freight, 322 shipments) were dropped before modelling; see data/processed/audit_duplicate_rows.csv.
Planning-time features only; total_qty, n_lrs and n_routes excluded because they are the outcome of loading.
Classes are imbalanced (about 9% under-loaded); judge on PR-AUC.

Counterfactual saving is indicative: V1 is a market-median price, capacities come from training history on the same route, and shipments on routes without a suitable training capacity are not covered.
RandomForest fitted on a 50,000-row training sample.
